facts.fact: The ICT minister Tatenda Mavetera announced that Zimbabwe's National Disability Policy and National ICT Policy would be reviewed to add accessibility guidelines, that every Community Information Centre must have a machine with braille software and assistive technology, and that the Universal Services Fund would subsidise assistive devices.
facts.system: National Disability Policy and National ICT Policy review

facts.fact: The Government launched the National Assistive Technology Strategy and Assistive Products Priority List on 24 May 2024, covering devices such as braille displays and speech-generating devices.

The Herald says the National ICT Policy (2022-2027) requires Government digital platforms to progressively meet international accessibility standards, and that advocates see few enforceable standards.

Permanent Secretary Kunaka says Government has set a target that by 2027 all new public service digital platforms comply with minimum accessibility standards, and that pre-procurement accessibility assessments are under discussion.
The Ministry of Health and Child Care launched the National Assistive Technology Strategy and the Assistive Products Priority List in May 2024.

Permanent Secretary Kunaka says Government, with ministries and partners, is implementing programmes that provide hearing aids, visual aids and other assistive technologies, with no number reached given.
